Mid-fraternal stature deviation reflects normal distribution around a mean, modeled as Gaussian noise with regression toward the mean. Eye color frequency across generations follows a Markov process, where each generation's trait distribution depends only on the previous one. Genetic contribution matrices encode Mendelian inheritance as linear transformations, enabling prediction of offspring traits. Failure modes include violation of independence assumptions, non-Mendelian inheritance, or environmental interference. Dualities emerge between deterministic trait propagation and stochastic variation. The regression framework underpins both prediction and retrodiction of hereditary outcomes.
